facts.text: The resort sits on a peninsula surrounded by Savusavu Bay.
facts.excerpt: Nestled on a peninsula surrounded by Savusavu Bay

facts.text: The resort is on Vanua Levu, Fiji's northern island, near the town of Savusavu.
facts.excerpt: The Jean-Michel Cousteau Resort is located on the northern Fijian island of Vanua Levu, with Savusavu, the closest larger town to the resort, home to Savusavu Airport (SVU).

facts.text: International flights arrive at Nadi, then guests take a domestic flight to Savusavu.
facts.excerpt: From Nadi, you take a domestic flight to Savusavu (SVU).

facts.text: A resort representative transfers guests from Savusavu Airport, a 20-minute drive.
facts.excerpt: a Jean-Michel Cousteau Resort Representative will transfer you to the resort, just a 20-minute drive away.

facts.text: Guests stay in traditional Fijian-style bures suited to couples or families.
facts.excerpt: our traditional Fijian-style Bures offer a luxurious retreat, perfect for couples or families.

facts.text: The Oceanfront Point Reef Spa Tub Bure has a private spa tub on the deck with views of Point Reef Beach.
facts.excerpt: Step onto the deck to enjoy a private Spa Tub with breathtaking views of Point Reef Beach.

facts.text: The Premium Oceanfront Two-Bedroom Villa has its own pool and spa tub.
facts.excerpt: 2nd bedroom with ensuite: 2 single day beds. Pool and Spa Tub

facts.text: The Oceanfront Point Reef Bures have a split-level design.
facts.excerpt: these Bures are among our most exclusive retreats due to the split-level design

facts.text: Divers can visit the Namena Marine Reserve, known for coral biodiversity, large fish populations, hawksbill turtles and seasonal whale migrations.
facts.excerpt: Encounter exceptional coral biodiversity, large fish populations, hawksbill turtles, and seasonal whale migrations.

facts.text: Weather permitting, Namena Marine Reserve is a 45-minute boat ride from the resort.
facts.excerpt: Weather permitting, the resort is just a 45-minute boat ride from Namena Marine Reserve

facts.text: The dive team has more than a dozen dive sites within a 15-minute boat ride.
facts.excerpt: they have more than a dozen spectacular dive sites within a 15-minute boat ride to choose from

facts.text: Resident marine biologists lead snorkeling expeditions and presentations on Savusavu Bay's marine ecology.
facts.excerpt: bring Savusavu Bay’s vibrant marine ecology to life through thrilling snorkeling expeditions and engaging presentations.

facts.text: The Golden Nugget site is a calm, shallow protected area suited to snorkelers.
facts.excerpt: Within moments, explore a serene protected area ideal for snorkelers. Discover colourful reef fish and diverse marine species in calm, shallow waters.

facts.text: The Dreamhouse dive site has barracudas, grey reef sharks and white tip sharks and is recommended for seasoned divers.
facts.excerpt: Dreamhouse lures with barracudas, grey reef sharks, and white tip sharks. Recommended for seasoned divers.

facts.text: The resort offers a PADI certification course.
facts.excerpt: PADI Certification Course

facts.text: The Kids Bula Club is free for all guests.
facts.excerpt: the Kids Bula Club is free for all our guests

facts.text: The Kids Bula Club offers Fijian crafts, guided snorkeling trips and eco-education.
facts.excerpt: The Kids Bula Club offers supervised activities such as: Fijian crafts, guided snorkeling trips, and eco-education for younger children.

facts.text: A teen program offers reef conservation, cultural storytelling and waterfall hikes.
facts.excerpt: The Teen Program engages teenagers in adventures like reef conservation, cultural storytelling and waterfall hikes.

facts.text: Families with children under five are assigned a pair of nannies.
facts.excerpt: Families with children under the age of five are assigned a pair of nannies

facts.text: The resort describes itself as Fiji's first luxury eco-resort.
facts.excerpt: As Fiji’s first luxury Eco-Resort, we are deeply committed to sustainability, marine conservation and authentic Fijian hospitality.

facts.text: Jean-Michel Cousteau, son of ocean explorer Jacques Cousteau, discovered the property in the 1980s and gave the resort his name.
facts.excerpt: Jean-Michel Cousteau, son of renowned ocean explorer Jacques Cousteau, discovered the property in the 1980s, found an investor, and gave the resort his name.

facts.text: The resort's design is inspired by a traditional Fijian village.
facts.excerpt: The overall resort design is inspired by a traditional Fijian village.

facts.text: The bures have thatched roofs and vaulted, exposed-beam ceilings with woven magimagi, a coconut fiber rope.
facts.excerpt: Vaulted, exposed beam ceilings feature woven magimagi (coconut fiber rope)

facts.text: The bures have no phones or televisions, but there is Wi-Fi.
facts.excerpt: None of the bures have phones or televisions, but there is Wi-Fi.

facts.text: The beachfront spa bure has two oceanfront, open-air treatment rooms.
facts.excerpt: With only a pair of oceanfront, open-air treatment rooms, the beachfront spa bure is teeny

facts.text: The spa offers traditional Fijian Bobo massage.
facts.excerpt: the art of traditional Fijian Bobo massage

facts.text: Yoga is typically offered twice a day on a seaside yoga platform.
facts.excerpt: Yoga practice is typically offered twice a day at the seaside yoga platform.

facts.text: In early 2026 the resort closed for just over two months for a renovation covering accommodations, the restaurant and bar, and the kids club.
facts.excerpt: In early 2026, the resort closed for just over two months for a nearly $10-million renovation that touched everything from accommodations to the restaurant and bar to the kids club.

facts.text: There is one restaurant with two open-air, ocean-view dining rooms, one for families and one for adults only.
facts.excerpt: Though there is only one restaurant, there are two open-air, ocean-view dining rooms—one for families and another for adults only.

facts.text: A traditional Fijian lovo feast is prepared once a week.
facts.excerpt: A traditional Fijian Lovo feast is prepared once a week

facts.text: The resort is set on 17 acres overlooking Savusavu Bay, less than a 15-minute drive from downtown Savusavu.
facts.excerpt: Set on 17 acres overlooking Savusavu Bay, the resort is less than a 15-minute drive from downtown Savusavu.

facts.text: The Bula Club area has three pools and a treehouse.
facts.excerpt: Bula Club kids have a generous stretch of the property—with a trio of pools and a stellar treehouse

facts.text: There are no adapted bures, but paths are paved and ramps reach public areas.
facts.excerpt: There are no adapted bures, but guests can request rooms close to the central area of the resort. Paths throughout the property are paved, and ramps provide access to public areas

facts.text: The resort is all-inclusive.
facts.excerpt: Discover our all inclusive resort

facts.text: A mangrove restoration project can be seen along the beach.
facts.excerpt: Take a walk along the beach past Bure 25 for a glimpse of the mangrove restoration project.

facts.text: Namena trips usually leave in the morning and can be bumpy.
facts.excerpt: Trips set out in the morning, typically at 7:30 a.m., and can be bumpy.

facts.text: Snorkelers can go to Namena Marine Reserve when conditions allow.
facts.excerpt: When conditions cooperate, the dive center also takes snorkelers to Namena Marine Reserve.

facts.text: After Cyclone Winston in 2016, the grounds team propagated more than 10,000 native flowering, fruiting and medicinal plants.
facts.excerpt: In 2016, after Cyclone Winston devastated the resort’s landscaping, the grounds team propagated more than 10,000 native flowering, fruiting, and medicinal plants
